This is England’s first multi-Test series win since December 2024. England have won their last five Tests at Lord’s; their last defeat came here in the 2023 Ashes.
Pakistan lost at Lord’s for the first time since 2010, after consecutive Test wins here in 2016 and 2018. Pakistan’s last Test series win in England came in 1996.
Pakistan have gone winless in their last 18 Tests in SENA countries since 2018, losing 16 and drawing two. Their last such win came at Lord’s in May 2018.
This is the first time in their Test history Pakistan have been bowled out for under 200 in four successive innings.
The false-shot percentage in this Test is 32.7% - the second-highest in a Test in England since ball-by-ball data is available, behind 32.9% in the ENG-SA match at The Oval in 2022.

Two convincing wins and Joe Root's new term as England's captain has begun really well. But he'll be the first to accept that his team and his captain was never tested, neither at Headingley nor here at Lord's. Pakistan were abject in both games and it's the batting which has let their team down. They'd have had some hopes with Babar Azam's return, but the skipper ended the match with scores of 6 and 8 - 14 in all, his lowest aggregate in a Test since January 2025, when batting in both innings. Conditions were admittedly tough, but they didn't give themselves a chance. It didn't help that Imam-ul-Haq was ruled out with a calf tear, but they were clearly second best across all three departments of the game. They've been battered and bruised, can they avoid a series whitewash in Birmingham? We've a break and we'll all be back on the 9th of September for the final Test of the English summer. For now, cheers and bye..
